newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece asks Albania to free jailed Socialist.
newsitem.headline: Greece asks Albania to free jailed Socialist.

text.p: Greece, concerned with the violence that has gripped Albania, said on Tuesday it would officially request its northern Balkan neighbour to free jailed opposition Socialist leader Fatos Nano.
International human rights groups have also called on the Albanian government to free Nano, saying his conviction was wrong and politically motivated.

"We have repeatedly asked the Albanian government and President (Sali) Berisha personally -- as I have myself -- to release the Socialist Party leader, Mr Fatos Nano," Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos told reporters.
"It is a request that we will repeat today through our ambassador, who will lodge a demarche with the Albanian government and President Berisha," he added.
Nano, who served a short term as prime minister in 1991, was arrested in 1993 and jailed a year later on charges of corruption relating to an Italian aid scandal.

He was recently transferred to Tirana from a prison in the southern Albanian town of Tepelene, where violence erupted two weeks ago over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes that left thousands of Albanians destitute.
Faced with a growing revolt in the south, Berisha agreed to form a new all-party government and hold early elections.
